support.p:
Script: 'bru tsha.
Lines per folio: 10.
Orthography:
- Bindu for m
- Numerals used for numbers and for phonetic value (e.g., 4+n for bzhin)
Some gaps in the lines, where glosses linked to a previous lines are written (see fol. 2b) suggest that the copyist copied a version of the text together with the annotations.
On fols. 3a and 3b, some numerals above portions of the text.

person.persName: dge slong blo ldan shes rab
rngog dge slong blo ldan shes rab
person.note:
See [BAQ9MH4T]: 193 for the main events of his life.
Three manuscript editions of his writings and translations were deposited respectively in rNgog Blo ldan shes rab's tomb, in the monastery of gSang phu (probably in the main assembly hall), and in Drin las kyi sde (ID:4357) ([7FZ3B926]: 107).

person.persName: zhang tshe spong chos kyi bla ma
zhang tshes spong chos kyi bla ma
tshes spong ba chos kyi bla ma
zhang tshe spong pa chos kyi bla ma
ne'u thog pa chos kyi bla ma
person.note: Third abbot of gSang phu ne'u thog monastery. Author of several commentaries, see [R894SIKE]: 405 (zhang tshe spong ba chos kyi bla mas kyang TI ka 'ga' re brtsams). Part of the group of the four main disciples of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) exX0032026-09-0202-25-28 .

His dates can be approximated as 1070-1130.
He is possibly the same person as Byang 'chad khyung (ID:6382), as [NA9AMDH6] states that Khyung rin chen grags held Byang 'chad (ID:4416) and taught Sa chen (ID:4205) there ([647FFPZR]: 543). [CJ75QQKN]: 339 (fol. 8a/170a1-3). dMar ston's Zhib mo rdo rje ([RA3FK3BK]: 134 and 137), on the other hand, distinguish the two figures and places Sa chen's studies with Khyung at Nyang stod byang 'chad, and those with Khyung rin chen grags at Nyang stod.
On the reference to Khyung as "slang pa/slang pha/slang pha ba" (understood as a regionalism for "glang pa/glang pha ba," see [WL39GVT5]: 940.

person.persName: gangs pa she'u blo gros byang chub
lum pa ba ye shes byang chub
person.note:
A funerary sa 'bum was erected in 'Ban grong to house his full body (see [647FFPZR]: 544, based on [Q3KCZX7B]: 43 and 92).
Possibly identical with "dge bshes gangs pa" alias Lum pa ba Ye shes byang chub (fl. late 11th and early 12th c.) ([CCSBSVCA] : 420, n. 25).
Expert in both scholastic and tantric traditions (exX0032026-04-2303-57-49 ).

person.note: Dates according to [2V6H2FBU]: 24, n. 70 ("Since Ar was invited as a dge bshes to a monastery in 1076, it is hard to believe that he was not at least 20 years old, which would put his birth-date at least in 1056. The last trace of his existence is in 1144 when he took over the head of rgyal lha khang.").

person.persName: zul phul bya 'dul ba 'dzin pa chen po
person.note: Born in 1091 at gTsang rong gyung and died at the age of 76 in Zul phu according to [R894SIKE]: 109. [W4T5ZMUP]: 38 accordingly proposes the dates 1091-1166. [VKBZTBWN], fol. 3b6 reports that he was born the year rNgog lo (ID:3786) came back to Tibet, i.e., ca. 1092. On his life, based on the Zul phu mkhan byang chub rin chen dpal bzang po'i rnam par thar pa (ID:6715), see [W4T5ZMUP]: 40. It is unclear whether he is the same person as rGya 'dul ba 'dzin pa (ID:4193). The [NA9AMDH6] distinguishes two "rGya 'dul 'dzin" - the elder (ID: 3941) and the younger (ID:4193) - and a "Bya 'dul 'dzin brTson 'grus 'bar" (student of 'Bre chen po). In contrast, the [R894SIKE] only mentions one "rGya 'dul 'dzin" (the elder), distinct from "Bya 'dul 'dzin" (who was ordained by 'Bre). [VKBZTBWN], fol. 6b5-6 and [8VLVHDR2], fol. 14b5 report that he was ordained by 'Bre and received from him the name in religion brTson 'grus 'bar. A number of the same teachers are mentioned for rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger and Bya 'dul 'dzin but, for instance, the latter's studies with rGya 'dul 'dzin the older took place when he was a retired abbot, whereas the former's studies with him took place when he was still abbot. Further, rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger became abbot of dGa' ba sdong and Bya 'dul abbot of Zul phu. This suggests they might have been distinct persons.

person.persName: phywa pa chos kyi seng ge
phya pa chos seng ge ba
dge' slong chos kyi seng ge
dge bshes chen po phya pa chos kyi seng ge
slob dpon phya pa chos kyi seng ge
slob dpon cha pa chos kyi seng ge
rigs pa'i dbang phyug phya pa
rigs pa'i dbang phyug chos kyi seng ge
mkhas pa chen po cha pa
person.note:
The majority of the information available on Phya pa has been provided in [EZ5JXHJY] and [8S7FDMCJ]. Summaries of the same are also found in [LQZU66YX]: 37-40, [F4UK2S8P]: 2-3, and [BW9UR427]: 35-36 (in French).
On his birth in 1109, the year of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786)'s passing, see [TM8DW8WA]: 32-33, [VKBZTBWN]: 4b4-5, and [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b2-3. On the date of his passing in a "sa mo glang" year, see [R894SIKE]: 400, [VKBZTBWN]: 4b4-5 and 6a5. [95UZA9Y5]: 40/3/5 (reported in [7FZ3B926]: 111 and [MPRU5QUC]: 206) specifies the day "sa mo glang gi lo'i nag pa zla ba nag po'i phyogs kyi tshes brgyad," i.e., on the 23rd of the third month.
A list of his students is provided in [EZ5JXHJY]: 356, based on [MQB8JGAX]: 297/4, [KL9XTQWI]: I, 454, [4YEPFBIB]: 340-341, [8GL7ZT7Y], fol. 15b3, [VKBZTBWN], fol. 4b7-5a4. [FDEWZ2NZ]: 290 also mentions the list of the four "jo sras" from bSod nams dpal's Bla ma rngog pa yab sras rim par byon pa’i rnam thar rin po che’i rgyan gyi phreng ba.
'Gos lo tsa ba lists numerous works composed before Phya pa took the see of gSang phu; these include commentaries and summaries on the Five works of Maitreya, the Pramāṇaviniścaya, the Satyadvayavibhaṅga, Madhyamakālaṃkāra, Madhyamakāloka, and Bodhicaryāvatāra. He mentions having seen these, the Yid kyi mun sel (ID:4503) and summaries on Madhyamaka, as well as (ID:4505) and (ID:5971). See exX0032026-04-2304-02-58 . 'Gos lo tsa ba does not mention any composition dealing with monastic discipline.
Śākya mchog ldan ([TM8DW8WA], 12-13 and 32) mentions a (doubtful) commentary on the Pramāṇavārttika (ID:3772) in addition to the commentary on the Pramāṇaviniścaya, and three summaries (small, intermediate, large), the intermediate one being the Yid kyi mun sel (ID:4503). (Discussed in [EZ5JXHJY]: 357, translated in [8S7FDMCJ]: 59).
Four groups of students are mentioned in Tibetan sources (which do not imply that the members of the respective groups were studying with Phya pa at the same time), with occasional variations:
1) The "Eight Great Lions" (seng chen brgyad). Eight scholars whose names contains the expression "seng ge," likely connoting their expertise in epistemology. The standard list includes gTsang nag pa (ID:3839), Dan 'bag (ID:3840), 'Bru sha (ID:3841), rMa bya (ID:3842), rTsags/rTsegs (ID:4289), Myang/Nyang bran (ID:3844), and gNyal pa/dMyal ma (ID:6679). The eighth one is instead sometimes said to be gTsang pa 'Jam dpal (ID:6336), 'U yug pa (ID:3846), or mTshur ston (DI:4315).
2) The "four sons of noble families" (jo sras mi bzhi) or the "three sons of noble families" (jo sras gsum). They are young noble men of the rNgog (ID:3847), 'Khon (ID:3848), Khu (ID:3849), and gNyos/sMyos (ID:3850). The four are listed in [VKBZTBWN]: 4a7 and [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b3, whereas on 16a1 the author speaks of "jo sras gsum." The four are also listed by bSod nams dpal, see [FDEWZ2NZ]: 290.
3) The "three wise ones" (shes rab can mi gsum) or "four wise ones" (shes rab can mi bzhi). The threefold-list in [VKBZTBWN]: 5a1 has rKong po (ID:3852), lHo pa sgom gzan (ID:3853), Par bu ba/sPar phu ba (ID:3854). 'Gar dbang grub (ID:3851) is added in the fourfold list, e.g. in [R894SIKE]: 406.
4) The "three accomplished ones" (grub thob mi gsum). These are students who later became famous masters: Dus gsum mkhyen pa (ID:3855), Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856), gSal sto (ID:3857). The third is sometimes replaced by Zhang tshal (ID:6409), or is suggested to be the latter's direct student.

person.note: Van der Kuijp ([H9MPLMTV]) proposed the dates (?-1185). The terminus ante quem for gTsang nag pa's death was pushed to 1192 by Schwabland ([Q8WU9EDW]: 794, n. 3) on account of the date of Khro pu lo tsA ba (ID:3878)'s studies with gTsang nag pa. This date was corrected to 1195 based on Khro phu lo tsA ba's biography (van der Kuijp, personal communication).

person.persName: dan bag pa smra ba'i seng ge
smra ba'i seng ge dan 'bag pa
dan phag pa dar ma seng ge
smra ba'i seng ge dar 'bag pa
person.note: Part of the group of Phya pa (ID:3831)'s students referred to as the "Eight Mighty Lions." Possibly identical with (ID:6217) ([4LWBNM7B]: 106). Maybe the same person as the "Chos kyi grags pa" mentioned as lineage successor of gTsang nag pa (ID:3839) and predecessor of gNyal zhig (ID:3887) in Bu ston's lineage of the Pramāṇaviniścaya (ID:3774).

person.persName: rma bya rtsod pa'i seng ge
person.note: rMa bya's name is rendered in Tangut as Po tjɨj ˑjɨr, in which po tjɨj is a phonetic transcription of "bodhi" [=Tib. byang chub], whereas ˑjɨr means "diligence" [=Tib. brtson 'grus].

person.persName: nyang bran pa chos kyi ye shes
person.note: Maybe the same person as "Nyang bran chos kyi seng ge" (ID:3844), as suggested in [CCSBSVCA]: 164, n. 416. However, A khu ching distinguishes the two. Author of manuals on the Śīkṣāsamuccaya (ID:3742) - see (ID: 6558) - and Bodhicaryāvatāra (ID: 3727). See [R894SIKE]: 405 (zhang tshe spong ba chos kyi bla mas kyang TI ka 'ga' re brtsams shing de'i slob ma nyan bran pa chos kyi ye shes kyis ni bslabs pa kun las btus pa dang | byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa la sogs pa spyod phyogs kyi yig cha dang |) and [EG6VZ8JK]: 26, translated from [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b2 (chos kyi ye shes kyis bslab spyod sogs byang chub sems dpa’i sde sogs la bshad nyan yun ring zhing rnam bshad mang po mdzad ).
Based on their dates, he is a different person than Khu le'i kha mo ze'u ston, Chu mig pa shes rab grags (ID:3975).

person.persName: khro phu lo tsA ba byams pa dpal
gnubs lo tsA ba byams pa'i dpal
person.note: [CTQMVBPR]: 37-38 an n. 40 reports that two dates are given in the [R894SIKE] for his birth: 1172 (given directly and can be inferred from the age given for him at the time of the birth of Chag lo (ID:6412) and 1173. [R894SIKE]: 828 sets his birth in a water female serpent year (1173), three years after the passing of Phag mo gru pa (ID:3856) (in 1170). Active as a translator, he invited the three Indian paṇḍitas Śrījagatamitrānanda, alias Mitrayogin, Buddhaśrījñāna (ID:5830), and Śākyaśrī (ID:6418) to Tibet ([2X2E3882]: 253).

person.persName: snar thang mkhan po a rmi ta kir ti
gro mo che ba bdud rtsi grags
person.note: Fourth abbot of sNar thang (ID:4411). On his life see [NTGHCZA8]: 34-51.

Same person as gTsang nags phug pa 'jam dbyangs shes rab 'od zer (ID:6640)? Late 13th-early 14th c. according to van der Kuijp ([H9MPLMTV]: 22). Late 12th-early 13th c. according to [MX3PRVV2]: 3/16 and n. 4. Considered to be identical with gNyal zhig's student 'Jam dbyangs gsar ma ([4LWBNM7B]: 121). Important master in the Dro lineage of the Kālacakra ([MX3PRVV2]). A list of his compositions is discussed in [MX3PRVV2]: 7-8/16.

person.persName: chos grags gnyis pa gzhon nu rin chen
chos grwa gsar ma gzhon nu rin chen
person.note: Fl. late 13th to early 14th c. We assume that the gZhon nu rin chen who was abbot of gSang phu is the same person as the author of the two works by gZhon nu rin chen. The latter is characterized in [8H6M69W4], No. 15506, as the "student of Nyang" (nyang gi slob ma), which, in view of the colophon of (ID:4625), is Nyang bran pa Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) rather than Nyang bran pa Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3844).

person.persName: bcom ldan rigs pa'i ral gri
person.note: On his career, see [KHA9ZVGP]: 3-8. The dates 1227-1305 are known from the biography (see work (ID:7016)) composed by his student bSam gtan bzang po (ID:4005) ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3). His name in religion was Dar ma rgyal mtshan or Chos kyi rgyal mtshan ([FZ6N88AU]: 406) - the name Chos kyi rgyal mtshan is given as his "real name" (mtshan dngos) in a homage by Rong ston ([KM47ZZDJ]: 657 and n. 62). The majority of the colophons of his works name him "bCom ldan ral gri," a few "Rigs/Rig pa’i ral gri" or just "Ral gri." Schwabland's discussion of the variants “Rigs pa” and “Rig pa” does not come to a definite conclusion as to which is the correct spelling ([CTQMVBPR]: 2-3). He was born as the son of a local wealthy headman, the fourth of five sons and his birth is reported to have been foretold by Śākyaśrībhadra (ID:6418) when he was invited by Ral gri's paternal uncle ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3).

person.note: Scholar associated with the Dwags po bKa' rgyud. [EZ5JXHJY]: 356 and n. 16 takes him to be the same person as gsal sto sho sgom (ID:3857), on of the three students of Phya pa (ID:3831) known as the "grub thob mi gsum."

Active in the 12th century in the intellectual tradition stemming from Phya pa (ID:3831). Possibly identical with (ID: 6219), the third abbot of sPyan yas (ID:6220). See [HZARCY3E]. Possibly identical with Dan bag pa smra ba'i seng ge (ID: 3840). See [4LWBNM7B]: 106.

bibl.author: gtsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge
bibl.note:
Extensive commentary spanning 210 folios in instance (ID:4549), including as well numerous excursuses. The author discusses the views of numerous Tibetan opponents who are not identifies by name (ca. 160 occurrences of "kha cig" in the work).
It corresponds to the work listed by A khu shes rab rgya mtsho in the Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9]: 539, No. 11807: gtsang nag pa'i rnam nges Tik chen).
See [H9MPLMTV] for an introduction to the work, its author, and the manuscript.

bibl.author: gtsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge
bibl.note:
The work is different from (ID:6860), an untitled work the incipit of which suggests a similar title as the present one.
This may correspond to the work listed by A khu ching shes rab rgya mtsho in his Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9]: 514, No. 11066: gtsang nag pa'i (bslab btus dang) spyod 'jug (gnyis) kyi 'grel pa).
The author refers to the views of other Tibetan scholars, some of whom are identified in glosses in (ID:4558), notably rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) ex013052025-11-2711-02-54, ex013052025-11-2711-06-32 , Ar Byang chub ye shes (ID:3816) ex013052025-11-2711-10-15 , rGya dmar ba (ID:3834) ex013052025-11-2711-18-04 , possibly Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) ex0130152025-11-2711-08-09 .

sdom pa nyi shu ba'i 'grel pa
bibl.author: gtsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge
bibl.note: Commentary on the Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃśaka (ID:3759), with some references to the views of other scholars, who are identified in interlinear annotations in (ID:4560). These including rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) ex013062025-11-2709-58-17 , Phya pa (ID:3831) ex013062025-11-2709-31-56 , "byang chub bzang po" (possibly Ar Byang chub ye shes (ID:3816)) ex013062025-11-2709-14-07 , and possibly Nyang bran Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) ex013062025-11-2709-31-46 . For a scholar referred to as "dam pa kha 1" in the text, an annotation glosses "khag sor ba" ex013062025-11-2709-31-59, and for an unidentified "kha 1" an annotation glosses "rgya mtsho 'phrind" ex013062025-11-2709-07-34 .

bibl.title: byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i spyi don
བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པའི་སྤྱི་དོན

byang chub sems bskyed spyi don
bibl.author: gtsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge
bibl.note:
General instruction on the generation of bodhicitta.
The author refers to the views of other scholars and bla mas who are not named in the text. Some of them are identified in glosses in (ID:4562); these include rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) ex013172025-11-2620-55-08 and Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) ex013172025-11-2620-55-18 , as well as the "three brothers" (sku mched gsum" ((ID:3829), (ID:7093), (ID:3830)) ex013072025-11-2708-17-15 . "Jo bo/Jo bo rje" (i.e., Atiśa (ID:3745)) is named in the main text - ex013072025-11-2621-00-59, ex013172025-11-2620-55-28, ex013072025-11-2708-20-45, ex013072025-11-2622-23-20 - and in an annotation ex013072025-11-2621-47-30 .

bibl.title: skyabs 'gro ba'i spyi don
སྐྱབས་འགྲོ་བའི་སྤྱི་དོན

skyabs 'gro'i spyi don
skyabs su gro'i spyi don
bibl.author: gtsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge
bibl.note:
General instruction on taking refuge, divided int three main sections: (1) the necessity of taking refuge, (2) ascertaining the nature of taking refuge, and (3) accomplishing the purpose of taking refuge.
The author notably refers to the views of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) and Chos kyi ye shes (possibly (ID:3876)); their name is given in glosses in (ID:4564): see ex013082025-11-2616-12-29, ex013082025-11-2616-12-29 .

bibl.title: spyod 'jug gi legs bshad bsdus pa
སྤྱོད་འཇུག་གི་ལེགས་བཤད་བསྡུས་པ
spyod 'jug gi bshad pa
bibl.author: gtsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge
bibl.note: The expression "legs bshad bsdus pa'i tshul" in the incipit recalls the title of gTsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge (ID:3839)'s commentary (ID:4559), but the contents are different. The author mentions that he summarizes the teachings of "rngog" (ID:3786), "phya pa" (ID:3831) and "nyang ran" (for nyang bran) (ID:3844) or (ID:3876) (both of whom wrote commentaries on the Bodhicaryāvatāra). The initial verses and part of the beginning of the text finds a literal equivalent in work (ID:4712) by Gro ston (ID:3880), who had been gTsang nag pa's student.

bibl.title: byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa'i bsdus don
བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་སྤྱོད་པ་ལ་འཇུག་པའི་བསྡུས་དོན
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa'i don
gtang nag pa'i spyod 'jug gi bsdus don
bibl.author: gtsang nag pa brtson 'grus seng ge
bibl.note: It is presumably a topical outline of the Bodhicaryāvatāra (ID:3727). An instance of this work in 5 folios is preserved at sNye mo Bye mkhar chos sde, see (ID:7059). The 7-folio instance entitled "spyod pa la 'jug pa'i don" (ID:7059) could also be an instance of that work ("don" for "bsdus don"?) or an incomplete manuscript of another work on the Bodhicaryāvatāra (ID:3727), see (ID:6860) and (ID:4559). The 13-folio "spyod 'jug gi sa bcad" ascribed to "brtson 'grus seng ge" (ID:7366) could be an instance of the same work.
